title: Laksa
subtitle: Malaysian coconut curry noodle soup with prawns
excerpt: Malaysia's most famous dish: rice noodles in a rich, fragrant coconut broth built on a paste of lemongrass, galangal, chilli, and shrimp paste, loaded with prawns, tofu, and bean sprouts, finished with lime and fresh herbs.

recipe.sourceNotes: Laksa is a spicy coconut-based noodle soup that is the most celebrated dish of the Peranakan (Straits Chinese) cuisine of Malaysia and Singapore. There are two main types: laksa lemak (also called Nyonya laksa), which uses coconut milk and is the most widely known internationally, and asam laksa, which uses a sour tamarind-based broth without coconut milk. The laksa lemak paste (rempah) is a complex mix of lemongrass, galangal, dried and fresh chilli, shallots, candlenuts, and belacan (shrimp paste). The soup is served with thick rice vermicelli, prawns, fishcake, tofu puffs, and bean sprouts, and finished with a squeeze of lime and laksa leaves (Vietnamese coriander). A good-quality bought laksa paste is an acceptable shortcut.

content.text: Fry the laksa paste in oil until it is very fragrant and the oil separates from the paste; this takes 5 to 8 minutes and is the most important step for developing the depth of flavour. Do not rush this stage. Add the coconut milk and stock gradually after the paste is fully cooked.

items.preparation: thick rice vermicelli; soaked in boiling water 5 minutes; drained
cut into cubes; shallow-fried until golden

content.text: Blend the lemongrass, galangal, chilli, shallots, garlic, turmeric, and paprika to a smooth paste in a blender with a splash of water.

Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring frequently, until very fragrant and the oil visibly separates. Add the coconut milk and stock. Bring to a simmer. Season with fish sauce. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink. Divide the noodles between bowls. Ladle over the broth and prawns. Top with bean sprouts, tofu, and coriander. Serve with lime wedges.
